name: Saodat Ferreira-Ulukhan
location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Saodat is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by decades of steam and spice smoke, her silver-streaked hair pinned under a faded yellow wrap she's worn so long it's become her trademark. Her left forearm is wrapped in a sleeve tattoo of a pepper vine that flowers whenever her skin temperature rises — a cheap bioink mod she got thirty years ago and has never seen reason to remove. She smells perpetually of fenugreek and charred chili, and her stall, a converted cargo container with a fold-out serving ledge, has been in the same spot in the Oxidian Market for twenty-two years. She speaks with the authority of a woman who has fed half of Geartown from infancy to old age.

Saodat is warmly domineering — she will decide what you are eating today, and you will thank her for it. She has strong opinions about everything from Zheng-Dao's latest transit fare hikes to which of her regulars is making poor romantic choices. Her memory for names, faces, and dietary restrictions is near-perfect, and she uses it like a gift. Beneath the maternal bluster is a woman who survived the displacement of Ironvein's old residential blocks twenty years ago and rebuilt her life around a single wok and a secondhand gas line.

core_fears: Being forced to leave her stall the way she was forced from Ironvein
Becoming irrelevant to the neighborhood she built herself into
core_desires: To ensure no one on her block goes hungry
To see the Vendors Guild gain formal legal recognition from the city council
blind_spots: Assumes her judgment about people is infallible
Underestimates how much she relies on the community for her own emotional stability
psychology.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing three families' rent for over a decade by skimming from her own Guild dues, and she keeps their names in a coded ledger she calls her 'recipe book.' She would be humiliated if anyone found out — not because it was wrong, but because she needs to be the one giving, not seen giving.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, warm, slightly formal Uzbek-inflected sentence structures blended with Geartown slang. Uses food metaphors constantly.
speech_patterns.cadence: Steady and unhurried, like someone who has never needed to rush to make a point.
verbal_tics: Clicking her tongue when she disapproves
Calling everyone 'my child' regardless of age
example_lines: 'Sit. I already know what you need and it is not what you think you came here for.'
'The Guild is not politics. The Guild is us deciding we exist on purpose.'

story_hooks: A Ferrogate Transit rezoning notice has appeared on her stall wall — her block is slated for 'infrastructure renewal' and she has eight weeks to vacate. She needs someone to dig up who actually filed the order.
One of her long-term subsidized families has gone silent. She's too proud to call it missing persons but she is frightened and wants someone discreet to check on them.
narrative_function: Community anchor and information hub — she knows everyone in Geartown by face if not name. Quest giver for neighborhood-level problems, emotional support NPC, rumor source with high reliability on local matters.
augmentations: Bioink tattoo sleeve (decorative, thermochromic). Reading lens implant in right eye for menus and pricing. No other augmentation.
daily_life: Arrives at her stall before dawn to prep broths and dry-roast spices, serves breakfast and lunch crowds, closes mid-afternoon, and spends evenings doing Guild paperwork or visiting sick neighbors.
affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (senior member)

decision_rules: Feed the person in front of you first, solve the problem second
Never betray a confidence told over a shared meal
Guild business stays in the Guild

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses quickly and either adopts or neutrally tolerates; rarely hostile to anyone who is hungry
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, occasionally overbearing, expresses love through unsolicited food and blunt advice

stress_responses.high: Delivers a calm, devastating monologue and then walks away to compose herself

contradictions: Preaches community interdependence but deeply resists asking for help herself
habits: Tastes every dish at least four times during prep
Leaves a small data offering at the E.L.F. shrine mounted inside her stall each morning
Keeps a written ledger in an analog notebook despite having a lens implant
breaking_points: Witnessing a child go hungry while someone nearby wastes food
Being lied to by someone she has fed and trusted

registered_firearms: Axiom Systems Biometric Lock Rifle BLR-3 'Personal'

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and sturdy, with the compact mass of someone who spends twelve hours daily on her feet at a cooking station. Forearms thick from decades of wok work, core strong. Not lean, but functional — every kilogram earned through labor.
physical_description.hair_style: Pinned back under a faded yellow cotton wrap, worn daily for twenty-two years until the fabric has softened to linen texture
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, right eye fitted with a reading lens implant (visible as faint amber tint in bright light)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep umber with warm undertones, darkened by sun exposure and decades of steam-kitchen work
physical_description.complexion: Face lined with expression — crow's feet from squinting at spice containers and smiling. Skin texture weathered but healthy, unmarked by acne or disease. Hands show burn scars (old, faded) on knuckles and inner wrists. No makeup. A small mole on her left cheekbone.
distinguishing_marks: Pepper vine sleeve tattoo wrapping her entire left forearm, rendered in thermochromic bioink that flowers into bloom when skin temperature rises from cooking heat or exertion — faint green vines that burst into red pepper blooms.
Network of thin burn scars across her inner wrists and the backs of both hands, accumulated over thirty years of wok work.
A long, pale scar running horizontally across her left shin, approximately eight centimeters, from a displacement-era accident during the Ironvein block evacuation twenty years ago.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Reading lens implant in right eye (visible as a faint amber-tinted pupil in bright ambient light, no obvious hardware). The thermochromic bioink tattoo on her left forearm is the only other visible modification, though it serves no augmented function—pure aesthetics and personal choice.
physical_description.posture_movement: She stands with weight distributed evenly, ready to move in any direction—muscle memory from a lifetime of kitchen work. Her walk is economical and deliberate, never rushed but never idle. When at rest, she leans against her stall counter with one hip, arms crossed, watching her workspace with the focus of a conductor. Her default expression is slightly skeptical, eyebrows raised, as if assessing whether you're making good life choices.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class, practical and worn. Her daily uniform: a faded yellow cotton wrap over her hair (same one for decades), a dark olive canvas apron stained with turmeric and soy sauce, and a loose linen tunic in cream or muted rust. Underneath, simple thermal base layer. On her feet: well-broken-in slip-on kitchen clogs, black synthetic, reinforced at the heel. A slim brass wedding band on her left ring finger, worn smooth. No jewelry otherwise—practical only. Her clothes smell permanently of fenugreek, charred chili, and woodsmoke.

image_prompt: A 58-year-old Central Asian woman with deep umber skin and silver-streaked dark hair pinned under a faded yellow cotton wrap, standing at a stall counter in a gritty cyberpunk food market. Her left forearm displays an intricate thermochromic pepper vine tattoo in deep greens and reds. She wears a turmeric-stained canvas apron over a loose cream linen tunic. Her expression is warmly commanding, slightly skeptical, with deep crow's feet from decades of squinting at cooking heat. Behind her, the Oxidian Market glows with neon signage and LED vendor lights reflecting off wet concrete. Steam rises from her converted cargo-container stall. Moody, warm amber lighting from cooking fires and market neon. Photorealistic, gritty, intimate portrait. --ar 2:3 --v 6
